message.content: The sky looks blue because air molecules scatter sunlight, especially the shorter blue wavelengths, much more strongly than longer red wavelengths (Rayleigh scattering). This scattered blue light reaches your eyes from all across the sky, so you see a blue “sky” rather than just the Sun’s direct light.
